# Introduction {#sec-intro}

This report establishes a deterministic stability guarantee for a residual
reinforcement-learning (RL) controller deployed on top of a nominal
nonlinear model-predictive controller (NMPC) and a model-based
disturbance observer (DOB). The combined NMPC--DOB layer is mature and
admits a classical stability certificate; the RL layer, by contrast, is a
neural-network policy and resists direct stability analysis.

Our strategy is to *borrow* the stability certificate of the baseline. We
first show that the NMPC--DOB cascade is *Input-to-State Stable* (ISS)
with respect to the uncompensated residual disturbance that escapes the
observer's passband. From the ISS inequality we extract a quantitative
budget on the admissible residual, then *map this budget back onto the RL
action space* as a hard, state-aware magnitude ceiling. Any RL torque
within the ceiling is admissible by construction; any torque exceeding
the ceiling is radially scaled back. The cage is built entirely from
quantities of the certified baseline, so the learning agent inherits a
provable stability margin without itself being verified.

The remainder of the document is organised as follows.
@sec-setup fixes notation and the cascade control law.
@sec-cascade introduces the three layers.
@sec-lyap states the standing assumptions that make the NMPC optimal cost
a valid Lyapunov candidate.
@sec-iss derives the baseline ISS inequality.
@sec-clip is the core contribution: the ISS-based action-clipping law and
its derivation via the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
@sec-estim describes how the three constants $c_x$, $\gamma_0$, and $r$
are obtained from simulation and hardware experiments.

# Setup and Notation {#sec-setup}

## Tracking-error state and the cascade control law

We work in the discrete-time tracking-error coordinates of the 6-DOF
manipulator. Let $\bm{q}_k,\bm{v}_k \in \mathbb{R}^6$ denote the measured
joint position and velocity at sample $k$, and let
$\bm{q}^{\mathrm{ref}}_k,\bm{v}^{\mathrm{ref}}_k$ be the time-varying
joint-space reference obtained by inverse kinematics of the Cartesian
end-effector target. The tracking-error state is

$$
\bm{x}_k \;\triangleq\;
\begin{bmatrix}
\bm{q}_k - \bm{q}^{\mathrm{ref}}_k \\[2pt]
\bm{v}_k - \bm{v}^{\mathrm{ref}}_k
\end{bmatrix}
\;\in\; \mathbb{R}^{12}.
$$ {#eq-state}

The origin $\bm{x}_k = \bm{0}$ denotes perfect tracking. Throughout this
document, $\|\,\cdot\,\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm.

The cascade control law executed by our implementation is

$$
\bm{u}_{\mathrm{cmd},k}
\;=\;
\underbrace{\bm{u}_{\mathrm{MPC},k}}_{\text{nominal NMPC}}
\;-\;
\underbrace{\bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k}}_{\text{DOB estimate}}
\;-\;
\underbrace{\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}}_{\text{residual RL}},
$$ {#eq-cmd}

where all three components live in the same physical joint-torque space
$\mathbb{R}^6$. The minus sign on the RL term reflects that the policy
is trained to *cancel* the residual disturbance, mirroring the DOB.

## Plant dynamics under the residual disturbance

Let $\bm{f}(\bm{x},\bm{u})$ denote the nominal (URDF-modelled) closed-loop
dynamics. The true plant, on real hardware or in simulation with friction
and base excitation, evolves as

$$
\bm{x}_{k+1} \;=\; \bm{f}\bigl(\bm{x}_k,\bm{u}_{\mathrm{cmd},k}\bigr)
\;+\; \bm{w}_k,
$$ {#eq-plant}

where $\bm{w}_k$ collects all sources of model mismatch (un-modelled
friction, base excitation, payload variation, parameter drift). The DOB
estimates the in-band component of $\bm{w}_k$ and subtracts it as
$\bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k}$; what the observer cannot capture remains
as the *residual disturbance*

$$
\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k} \;\triangleq\;
\bm{w}_k \;-\; \bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k}
\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^6.
$$ {#eq-dres-def}

The residual is the *only* exogenous input that appears in the
forthcoming ISS analysis. We will frequently abuse notation and write
$\bm{x}_{k+1} = \bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}} + \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$,
where $\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}$ is the disturbance-free successor
state under the nominal closed loop; this is the standard
state-displacement embedding of an input disturbance and is sufficient
for the Lyapunov analysis that follows.

# The Cascade Architecture {#sec-cascade}

## Layer 1 --- Nominal NMPC {#sec-nmpc}

The NMPC solves, at each sample $k$, a finite-horizon optimal-control
problem

$$
V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)
\;=\;
\min_{\bm{u}_{0:N-1}}
\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \ell\bigl(\bm{x}_{k+j},\bm{u}_{k+j}\bigr)
\;+\; V_f\bigl(\bm{x}_{k+N}\bigr)
$$ {#eq-vstar}

subject to the nominal dynamics $\bm{x}_{j+1}=\bm{f}(\bm{x}_j,\bm{u}_j)$,
input bounds, and (implicitly) a terminal set. The NMPC feedback law is
the first element of the minimising sequence,
$\bm{u}_{\mathrm{MPC},k} = \kappa_N(\bm{x}_k) \triangleq
\bm{u}^*_{0}(\bm{x}_k)$. In our implementation the stage cost is
$$
\ell(\bm{x},\bm{u}) \;=\;
Q_{\mathrm{pos}}\,\bigl\|\bm{p}(\bm{x})-\bm{p}^{\star}\bigr\|^2
+ Q_{\mathrm{vel}}\,\bigl\|\bm{v}(\bm{x})\bigr\|^2
+ R_{\tau}\,\|\bm{u}\|^2,
$$ {#eq-stage}
with $Q_{\mathrm{pos}}=5000$, $Q_{\mathrm{vel}}=10$, $R_{\tau}=0.1$,
horizon $N=8$, and sample time $\Delta t = 0.02$~s; $\bm{p}(\bm{x})$
denotes the forward-kinematics end-effector position.

The optimal cost $V_N^*$ defined in @eq-vstar will serve as our
Lyapunov candidate.

## Layer 2 --- Model-based DOB {#sec-dob}

The DOB estimates the disturbance from the dynamics residual:
$\bm{d}_{\mathrm{raw},k} = \mathrm{RNEA}\bigl(\bm{q}_k,\bm{v}_k,
\hat{\bm{a}}_k\bigr) - \bm{u}_{\mathrm{cmd},k-1}$,
where $\hat{\bm{a}}_k$ is an acceleration estimate (in simulation this is
the ground-truth physical acceleration; on hardware it is the finite
difference of $\bm{v}_k$). The raw estimate is passed through a
first-order low-pass filter with smoothing factor $\alpha \in (0,1)$:

$$
\bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k}
\;=\; (1-\alpha)\,\bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k-1}
\;+\; \alpha\,\bm{d}_{\mathrm{raw},k}.
$$ {#eq-dob-lpf}

The filter shapes which disturbances are cancelled and which fall through
to the residual @eq-dres-def. Reducing $\alpha$ tightens the passband,
which *enlarges* the residual that the RL layer must handle.

## Layer 3 --- Residual RL {#sec-rl}

The RL policy $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k} = \pi(\bm{o}_k)$ is a neural
network that observes the same signals available to the DOB plus the
DOB's output, and emits an additive joint torque whose ideal target is
the residual itself, i.e.
$\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k} \to \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$.
The policy is trained against a reward that penalises the residual
$\bm{d}_{\mathrm{eff},k} \triangleq \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k} -
\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}$ and tracking error.
Because $\pi$ is a learned, possibly stochastic, function, no closed-form
stability statement is available for the closed loop that includes it.
The role of @sec-clip is to provide one.

# Lyapunov Candidate: The Optimal NMPC Cost {#sec-lyap}

We adopt the NMPC value function $V_N^*$ from @eq-vstar as the
composite Lyapunov candidate for the cascade. This choice is standard in
the predictive-control literature and avoids the need to design a
Lyapunov function by hand.

## Standing assumptions

We collect the three structural assumptions used throughout the rest of
the document. They are the standard hypotheses behind the quasi-infinite
horizon NMPC stability theorem [@mayne2000; @rawlings2017], adapted to
our cascade setting.

::: {#asm-lyap}
**Standing assumptions on the operating domain and the NMPC value function.**

There exists a compact operating domain $\mathcal{X} \subset
\mathbb{R}^{12}$ containing the origin in its interior, such that on
$\mathcal{X}$ the following hold:

- **(A1) Lyapunov sandwich.** There exist $\alpha_1,\alpha_2 \in
  \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
  $\alpha_1(\|\bm{x}\|) \le V_N^*(\bm{x}) \le \alpha_2(\|\bm{x}\|)$
  for all $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$.

- **(A2) Quadratic stage-cost lower bound.** There exists $c_x>0$ with
  $\ell\bigl(\bm{x},\kappa_N(\bm{x})\bigr) \;\ge\; c_x\,\|\bm{x}\|^2$
  for all $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$.

- **(A3) Local Lipschitz continuity of $V_N^*$.** There exists
  $\gamma_0>0$ such that, for every $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ and every
  perturbation $\bm{\delta}\in\mathbb{R}^{12}$ with
  $\bm{x}+\bm{\delta}\in\mathcal{X}$,
  $\bigl|V_N^*(\bm{x}+\bm{\delta}) - V_N^*(\bm{x})\bigr|
  \;\le\; \gamma_0\,\|\bm{\delta}\|$.

:::

(A1)–(A3) are mild: (A1) follows from positive-definiteness and radial
unboundedness of the cost; (A2) is design-driven and is automatically
satisfied by the quadratic stage cost @eq-stage; (A3) holds locally
because $V_N^*$ is the value of a smooth, finite-horizon quadratic
program on a compact set.

The constants $c_x$ and $\gamma_0$ that appear in (A2)–(A3) are *exactly*
the two constants we will need to size the action-clipping law. How to
obtain them in practice is the subject of @sec-estim.

## Value-function descent (nominal stability) {#sec-vfdescent}

Under (A1)–(A2) and the standard NMPC terminal ingredients (a
control-invariant terminal set $\mathcal{X}_f \subset \mathcal{X}$ with a
local control-Lyapunov terminal cost $V_f$), the NMPC value function
satisfies the well-known *descent property* along the nominal closed
loop.

::: {#lem-descent}
**Lemma 1 (Value-function descent).**
Under @asm-lyap and the standard NMPC terminal assumptions, the optimal
cost $V_N^*$ satisfies
$$
V_N^*\bigl(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}\bigr) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)
\;\le\;
-\ell\bigl(\bm{x}_k,\kappa_N(\bm{x}_k)\bigr)
\;\le\;
-c_x\,\|\bm{x}_k\|^2
$$ {#eq-descent}
for every $\bm{x}_k \in \mathcal{X}$, where
$\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}} = \bm{f}\bigl(\bm{x}_k,\kappa_N(\bm{x}_k)\bigr)$
is the disturbance-free successor.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Proof sketch (standard)

The argument is the canonical "tail-shift" of NMPC stability theory
[@mayne2000, Thm. 1; @rawlings2017, §2.4]. From $\bm{x}_k$ the optimal
plan costs $V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)$ over $N$ steps. After applying its first
input the system reaches $\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}$; *re-using the
tail* of the previous plan and appending the terminal controller yields
a *feasible* (not necessarily optimal) plan from $\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}$
whose cost is at most $V_N^*(\bm{x}_k) - \ell(\bm{x}_k,\kappa_N(\bm{x}_k))$.
The re-optimised value $V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}})$ cannot exceed
this feasible cost, which proves the first inequality. Applying (A2)
proves the second.
:::

@lem-descent isolates the *intrinsic convergence strength* of the
controller: every disturbance-free step strips at least $c_x\|\bm{x}_k\|^2$
units of cost. The constant $c_x$ is the **convergence coefficient** of
the nominal loop and is the first ingredient of the action-clipping law.

# Input-to-State Stability of the Baseline {#sec-iss}

We now activate the residual disturbance and the DOB, keeping
$\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k} = \bm{0}$ (i.e., the *baseline* is the
NMPC--DOB cascade alone). The goal is to certify ISS of the baseline
with respect to $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$.

## Cost propagation under the residual disturbance

The true successor state under the residual disturbance is
$$
\bm{x}_{k+1} \;=\; \bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}
\;+\; \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}.
$$ {#eq-disturbed-succ}

The one-step change of the Lyapunov candidate decomposes by adding and
subtracting $V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}})$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)
&= \underbrace{\bigl[V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}
                 + \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k})
        - V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}})\bigr]}_{\text{perturbation term}}
\\[4pt]
&\quad+ \underbrace{\bigl[V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}})
        - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)\bigr]}_{\text{nominal descent term}}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-split}

This decomposition is an identity: nothing has been bounded yet. Its
purpose is to *isolate the only place the disturbance enters*—the first
bracket—from the part already controlled by @lem-descent.

## Lipschitz bound on the perturbation term

The first bracket of @eq-split is bounded directly by Assumption (A3):
$$
V_N^*\bigl(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}} + \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\bigr)
- V_N^*\bigl(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}}\bigr)
\;\le\; \gamma_0\,\bigl\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\bigr\|.
$$ {#eq-lip}

The constant $\gamma_0$ is the **disturbance gain** of the cascade. It
plays the role of an "exchange rate" from units of state displacement
(metres of error) to units of cost. A large $\gamma_0$ means the cost
landscape is steep near the operating trajectory and the system is
sensitive to small disturbances; a small $\gamma_0$ means the cost
surface is flat and the system is tolerant.

## The baseline ISS inequality

Combining @lem-descent and @eq-lip yields the central result of this
section.

::: {#thm-baseline-iss}
**Theorem 1 (Baseline ISS).**
Under @asm-lyap and the standard NMPC terminal assumptions, the
NMPC--DOB baseline cascade (i.e., @eq-cmd with $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL}}=\bm{0}$)
satisfies, on the operating domain $\mathcal{X}$,
$$
V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)
\;\le\;
-c_x\,\|\bm{x}_k\|^2
\;+\; \gamma_0\,\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|.
$$ {#eq-iss}
Equivalently, the baseline is *Input-to-State Stable* with respect to
the residual disturbance $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$, with ISS-Lyapunov
function $V_N^*$, dissipation rate $\alpha_3(s)=c_x s^2$, and disturbance
gain $\sigma(s)=\gamma_0 s$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Proof

The decomposition @eq-split is an identity. Bound its first bracket
using @eq-lip and its second using @eq-descent; sum the two bounds.
The resulting inequality @eq-iss matches the ISS-Lyapunov template of
Jiang & Wang [@jiang2001, Thm. 1], so ISS follows immediately. $\square$
:::

@eq-iss is the *quantitative* statement of stability. The first term on
the right is the energy *drain* due to the controller; it scales like
$\|\bm{x}_k\|^2$ and dominates far from the origin. The second term is
the energy *refill* due to the disturbance; it scales linearly with
$\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|$. Equilibrium between drain and refill sets
the steady-state radius of the tracking error.

# ISS-Based Action Clipping {#sec-clip}

We now use the budget hidden inside @eq-iss to constrain the RL action.
The argument proceeds in four steps: (i) extract the admissible
residual budget from the ISS inequality; (ii) write the ISS inequality
for the closed loop *with* the RL layer; (iii) impose a *preservation
criterion* that the RL action must not enlarge the residual it is meant
to shrink; (iv) reduce that criterion, via the Cauchy--Schwarz
inequality, to a hard magnitude ceiling on
$\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}$.

## The admissible residual budget {#sec-budget}

Fix a desired *practical convergence radius* $r > 0$: we want the
tracking error to settle inside $\|\bm{x}_k\| \le r$. From @eq-iss, the
cost stops contracting precisely when the drain no longer dominates the
refill, i.e. when $c_x\,\|\bm{x}_k\|^2 \le \gamma_0\,\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|$.
To force this balance to occur *at* or *inside* the target radius, the
refill at $\|\bm{x}_k\|=r$ must not exceed the drain there:
$$
\gamma_0\,\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\| \;\le\; c_x\,r^2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\| \;\le\; \bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}
\;\triangleq\; \frac{c_x\,r^2}{\gamma_0}.
$$ {#eq-budget}

::: {#def-budget}
**Definition 1 (Admissible residual budget).**
The scalar
$\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}} \triangleq c_x r^2 / \gamma_0$
is the **admissible residual budget**: the largest residual norm that
the baseline NMPC--DOB cascade can absorb while keeping the
tracking-error state within radius $r$.
:::

The three quantities entering @eq-budget have crisp roles:
$c_x$ rewards strong convergence (larger $c_x$ enlarges the budget),
$r$ rewards looser performance targets (the budget grows like $r^2$),
and $\gamma_0$ punishes sensitivity to disturbance (a steeper cost
surface shrinks the budget).

## ISS inequality with the RL layer active

With $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k} \ne \bm{0}$, the effective disturbance seen
by the baseline is shifted:
$$
\bm{d}_{\mathrm{eff},k}
\;\triangleq\;
\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k} - \bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k},
$$ {#eq-deff}
and the ISS inequality @eq-iss becomes
$$
V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)
\;\le\;
-c_x\,\|\bm{x}_k\|^2
\;+\; \gamma_0\,\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k} - \bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|.
$$ {#eq-iss-with-rl}

## The stability-preservation criterion

We declare that the RL layer is *admissible at step $k$* whenever it
does not enlarge the residual it is intended to cancel:
$$
\boxed{\quad
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k} - \bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|
\;\le\; \|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|.
\quad}
$$ {#eq-criterion}

If @eq-criterion holds, then @eq-iss-with-rl is *no worse* than @eq-iss,
so the baseline ISS certificate carries over verbatim and the closed
loop remains ISS with the same constants.

## From the preservation criterion to a magnitude bound {#sec-magbound}

@eq-criterion is geometric and depends on the unmeasurable internal
quantity $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$. We now reduce it to a *measurable*
condition on $\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|$ alone, in three algebraic
steps.

**Step 1 --- Square both sides.** Squaring @eq-criterion and expanding
the inner product on the left:
$$
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|^2
- 2\,\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\!\top}\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}
+ \|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|^2
\;\le\;
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|^2,
$$
which simplifies to
$$
\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|^2
\;\le\;
2\,\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\!\top}\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}.
$$ {#eq-squared}

**Step 2 --- Cauchy--Schwarz, with the known bound.**
The inner product on the right of @eq-squared depends on the
unmeasurable $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$. Writing
$\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\!\top}\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k} =
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|\,\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|\cos\theta$
with $\theta \in [0,\pi]$ the angle between the two vectors, the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives $\cos\theta \le 1$, and the residual
budget @eq-budget gives
$\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\| \le \bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}$. Together,
$$
\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\!\top}\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}
\;\le\;
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|\,\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|
\;\le\;
\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}\,\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|.
$$ {#eq-cs}

**Step 3 --- Solve for $\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|$.** Substituting
@eq-cs into @eq-squared,
$$
\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|^2
\;\le\;
2\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}\,\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|.
$$
Dividing both sides by $\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\| > 0$ (the case
$\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}=\bm{0}$ is trivial) yields the ceiling.

::: {#thm-ceiling}
**Theorem 2 (ISS action-magnitude ceiling).**
Suppose @asm-lyap holds and the baseline satisfies @thm-baseline-iss.
For any step $k$ at which the preservation criterion @eq-criterion is
demanded, the RL action magnitude must satisfy
$$
\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|
\;\le\;
2\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}
\;=\;
\frac{2\,c_x\,r^2}{\gamma_0}.
$$ {#eq-ceiling}
:::

## The clipping law {#sec-cliplaw}

The ceiling @eq-ceiling is enforced as a *stateless, radial* saturation
layer interposed between the actor network and the joint command. If
the raw output already satisfies the ceiling, it passes through
unchanged; otherwise it is scaled radially back onto the boundary of
the admissible ball:

::: {#def-clip}
**Definition 2 (ISS clipping law).**
The clipped RL torque applied to the cascade is
$$
\boxed{\quad
\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}^{\mathrm{clip}}
\;=\;
\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\cdot
\min\!\Bigl[\,1,\;
\frac{2\,c_x\,r^2}{\gamma_0\,\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\|}
\Bigr].
\quad}
$$ {#eq-clip}
:::

Two properties of @eq-clip deserve emphasis:

1. **Direction-preserving.** The scaling is radial, so a well-aimed but
   over-strong correction is *softened*, never *redirected*. This is
   important because the policy's reward function rewards alignment of
   $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL}}$ with $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res}}$; per-component
   clamping would destroy that alignment.

2. **Stateless.** The clip depends only on the constants $c_x,\gamma_0,r$
   (fixed once and for all) and on the current $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}$.
   It does not depend on the state $\bm{x}_k$ or on the residual
   $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$. This makes the clip cheap on hardware and
   trivial to implement.

## Geometric interpretation and honest caveat {#sec-geom}

@eq-ceiling is a *necessary* condition for @eq-criterion to be
satisfiable; it is **not** a blanket *sufficient* condition. Reading
@eq-squared exactly, the preservation criterion holds if and only if
$\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\| \le 2\,\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|\,\cos\theta$.
The largest value the right-hand side can take, over all admissible
residuals and all angles, is $2\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}$, attained only
when the action is *perfectly aligned* with the residual at the
worst-case magnitude. Thus $2\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}$ is the **outer
envelope**: any action exceeding it cannot satisfy @eq-criterion under
*any* alignment, and is therefore provably unsafe; the clip removes
exactly these actions.

Inside the envelope, alignment is the policy's job, not the clip's.
What the clip guarantees, even in the adversarial worst case where the
clipped action is *anti-aligned* with the residual, is a hard upper
bound on the effective residual via the triangle inequality:
$$
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{eff},k}\|
\;\le\;
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\| + \|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}^{\mathrm{clip}}\|
\;\le\;
\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}} + 2\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}
\;=\;
3\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}.
$$
Plugging $3\,\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}$ back into the ISS inequality @eq-iss
in place of $\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res}}\|$ shows that the closed loop
remains ISS with an enlarged—but still finite—ultimate radius
$\sqrt{3}\,r$. **The cage never opens.**

::: {.callout-tip}
## What the clip guarantees, in one sentence

If the RL policy aligns with the residual (its trained behaviour), the
error settles inside the target radius $r$; if the policy fails
arbitrarily, the error stays inside $\sqrt{3}\,r$.
:::

# Practical Estimation of the ISS Constants {#sec-estim}

The clipping law @eq-clip contains three constants: $c_x$, $\gamma_0$,
and $r$. This section explains how each is obtained.

## Convergence coefficient $c_x$ {#sec-estim-cx}

By Assumption (A2), $c_x$ is the largest scalar satisfying
$\ell(\bm{x},\kappa_N(\bm{x})) \ge c_x \|\bm{x}\|^2$. Equivalently, by
@lem-descent, $c_x$ is the largest scalar consistent with the
descent property
$$
\frac{V_N^*(\bm{x}_k) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{nom}})}
     {\|\bm{x}_k\|^2}
\;\ge\; c_x
\quad\text{for all nominal } \bm{x}_k\in\mathcal{X}.
$$ {#eq-cx-defn}

A nominal trajectory is one in which the disturbance is small or absent;
on real hardware we approximate "nominal" by *quiet* operating
conditions (no intentional disturbance, no external excitation, no
payload changes). The empirical estimator is then

::: {#def-cx-emp}
**Definition 3 (Empirical convergence coefficient).**
Let $\{(\bm{x}_k, V_N^*(\bm{x}_k))\}_{k=1}^{K}$ be a sequence of
state--cost pairs logged from quiet closed-loop operation. The empirical
convergence coefficient is the lower 5th percentile,
$$
\hat{c}_x \;=\;
\mathrm{percentile}_{5}\!\Biggl\{\;
\frac{V_N^*(\bm{x}_k) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1})}
     {\|\bm{x}_k\|^2}
\;:\;
\|\bm{x}_k\| > \epsilon,\;\;
V_N^*(\bm{x}_k) > V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1})
\;\Biggr\},
$$ {#eq-cx-emp}
where $\epsilon$ is a small floor (e.g.\ $10^{-3}\,$m) preventing the
ratio from exploding near the origin.
:::

The use of the 5th percentile rather than the strict minimum trades off
two competing concerns: the strict minimum is contaminated by isolated
numerical outliers (e.g.\ MPC solves that hit the iteration cap), while
the median over-estimates the descent and would violate the lower-bound
interpretation for a non-trivial fraction of samples. The 5th percentile
gives a *robust lower envelope* that is safe in the ISS sense (i.e.\ a
valid lower bound for $\ge 95\%$ of samples).

This procedure can be applied identically in simulation and on real
hardware. We recommend taking
$\hat{c}_x = \min(\hat{c}_x^{\mathrm{sim}},\hat{c}_x^{\mathrm{real}})$
to absorb the discrepancy caused by unmodelled friction on the physical
plant.

## Disturbance gain $\gamma_0$ {#sec-estim-gamma}

By Assumption (A3) and the construction of @eq-lip, $\gamma_0$ is the
smallest scalar that upper-bounds the cost change induced by a state
displacement of the magnitude of $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$.
Re-arranging the ISS inequality @eq-iss,
$$
\gamma_0 \;\ge\;
\frac{-\bigl[V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)\bigr]
       \;+\; c_x\,\|\bm{x}_k\|^2}
     {\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\|}
\quad\text{whenever } \|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}\| > 0.
$$ {#eq-gamma-defn}

The numerator is computable from logged $V_N^*$ and $\|\bm{x}_k\|$; the
denominator requires the *clean ground-truth residual*. This is the
critical practical asymmetry:

- **In simulation**, $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$ is computable exactly
  from $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{true},k}^{\mathrm{sim}} -
  \bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k}$, where the "true" disturbance is obtained
  by inverse dynamics with the ground-truth joint acceleration provided
  by the physics engine.
- **On real hardware**, the joint acceleration is reconstructed by
  finite differences, which injects numerical noise into the residual
  estimate. The empirical fit @eq-gamma-defn would *under-estimate*
  $\gamma_0$ (because the noisy denominator is inflated), which is the
  unsafe direction.

The remedy is to estimate $\gamma_0$ *in simulation only*, then transfer
the value to real hardware. The transfer is exact because $\gamma_0$ is
a property of the cost function $V_N^*$, and $V_N^*$ is the *same
mathematical function* in sim and real (same NMPC weights, same URDF,
same horizon, same sample time).

::: {#def-gamma-emp}
**Definition 4 (Empirical disturbance gain).**
Let $\{(\bm{x}_k, V_N^*(\bm{x}_k), \bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\mathrm{sim}})\}_{k=1}^{K}$
be logged from a baseline simulation run with the full disturbance
curriculum active. The empirical disturbance gain is the 95th
percentile,
$$
\hat{\gamma}_0 \;=\;
\mathrm{percentile}_{95}\!\Biggl\{\;
\frac{-\Delta V_k + \hat{c}_x\,\|\bm{x}_k\|^2}
     {\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\mathrm{sim}}\|}
\;:\;
\|\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}^{\mathrm{sim}}\| > \delta,
\;\;\text{(ratio)} > 0
\;\Biggr\},
$$
where $\Delta V_k = V_N^*(\bm{x}_{k+1}) - V_N^*(\bm{x}_k)$ and $\delta$
is a small floor preventing division by near-zero residuals.
:::

The 95th percentile—rather than the strict maximum—gives a *robust upper
envelope* in the same way the 5th percentile gave a robust lower
envelope for $\hat{c}_x$.

## Target radius $r$ {#sec-estim-r}

The radius $r$ is the *only* design quantity in the clipping law; it is
not measured but *selected*. It encodes the practical tracking accuracy
the user is willing to certify. Three observations guide the choice:

1. **The clip ceiling scales as $r^2$.** Halving $r$ shrinks the
   ceiling by a factor of four; doubling $r$ enlarges it sixteen-fold.
   Aggressive (small) $r$ yields a tighter guarantee but allows the RL
   layer almost no contribution; permissive (large) $r$ enlarges the
   guarantee region but lets the policy be more active.

2. **$r$ should be consistent with what the baseline can already
   achieve.** If the baseline NMPC--DOB tracking error is observed to
   settle around $\|\bm{x}_k\| \approx r_{\mathrm{base}}$ in steady
   state, then choosing $r \ll r_{\mathrm{base}}$ certifies an
   unattainable guarantee and forces the clip to be uselessly tight.
   A pragmatic choice is $r \approx r_{\mathrm{base}}$, or slightly
   smaller if the RL layer is expected to close the gap.

3. **$r$ does not appear in the ISS certificate of @thm-baseline-iss
   itself.** It only appears in the *budget* @eq-budget and the
   *ceiling* @eq-ceiling. ISS holds independently of $r$; the choice
   of $r$ only specifies *which* radius the budget targets.

## Hybrid sim--real workflow {#sec-estim-flow}

Putting the three estimators together:

| Constant            | Where measured                | Why                                       |
|---------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| $c_x$               | both, take $\min$             | property of NMPC + plant; real may be smaller due to friction |
| $\gamma_0$          | simulation only               | property of $V_N^*$ alone; transfers exactly to real          |
| $r$                 | design choice                 | not measured                              |

The final clip ceiling used at run-time is
$$
\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL}}\|
\;\le\;
\frac{2\,\hat{c}_x\,r^2}{\hat{\gamma}_0},
\qquad
\hat{c}_x = \min(\hat{c}_x^{\mathrm{sim}}, \hat{c}_x^{\mathrm{real}}),
\quad
\hat{\gamma}_0 = \hat{\gamma}_0^{\mathrm{sim}}.
$$ {#eq-final-clip}

Because the strict minimum of $c_x$ and the strict maximum form of
$\gamma_0$ are *both* taken in the conservative direction, all
estimation error is absorbed by a small reduction in the clip
ceiling. Stability is therefore preserved under estimation error; only
the RL layer's freedom is reduced. This is the desired robustness
property of the proposed certificate.

# Summary {#sec-summary}

Under the standing assumptions @asm-lyap, the NMPC--DOB cascade is ISS
with respect to the residual disturbance (@thm-baseline-iss), with
quadratic dissipation rate $c_x$ and linear disturbance gain $\gamma_0$.
For any target radius $r > 0$, the admissible residual budget
$\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}} = c_x r^2/\gamma_0$ specifies the largest
residual the baseline can absorb while keeping the tracking error inside
$r$. The residual RL layer is admissible at step $k$ if it does not
enlarge the residual it is meant to cancel; this preservation criterion
reduces, via the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, to the magnitude ceiling
$\|\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}\| \le 2 c_x r^2/\gamma_0$ (@thm-ceiling) and
the radial clipping law @eq-clip. Provably-unsafe actions—those whose
magnitude exceeds $2\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}}$ and cannot satisfy the
preservation criterion under any alignment—are removed by construction.
Inside the envelope, even adversarial misalignment of the clipped
action leaves the closed loop ISS with enlarged ultimate radius
$\sqrt{3}\,r$; the cage never opens. The three constants $c_x,
\gamma_0, r$ are obtained via @def-cx-emp, @def-gamma-emp, and the
design rule of @sec-estim-r; the resulting hybrid sim--real workflow
@eq-final-clip is robust to estimation error in the conservative
direction.

# Symbol Reference {.appendix}

| Symbol                                | Meaning                                                       |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| $\bm{x}_k \in \mathbb{R}^{12}$        | Tracking-error state (6 position errors + 6 velocity errors)  |
| $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{MPC},k}$             | Nominal NMPC torque, $\kappa_N(\bm{x}_k)$                     |
| $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{filter},k}$          | DOB low-pass-filtered disturbance estimate                    |
| $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}$              | Residual RL torque (pre-clip)                                 |
| $\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL},k}^{\mathrm{clip}}$ | RL torque after ISS clipping @eq-clip                      |
| $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res},k}$             | Residual disturbance (DOB out-of-band leftover)               |
| $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{eff},k}$             | Effective residual under RL, $\bm{d}_{\mathrm{res}}-\bm{u}_{\mathrm{RL}}$ |
| $V_N^*(\bm{x})$                       | NMPC optimal cost (Lyapunov candidate)                        |
| $\kappa_N(\bm{x})$                    | NMPC feedback law (first element of optimal sequence)         |
| $\ell(\bm{x},\bm{u})$                 | NMPC per-step stage cost                                      |
| $c_x > 0$                             | Convergence coefficient, stage-cost lower bound (A2)          |
| $\gamma_0 > 0$                        | Disturbance gain, local Lipschitz constant of $V_N^*$ (A3)    |
| $r > 0$                               | Target practical convergence radius                           |
| $\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}} = c_x r^2/\gamma_0$ | Admissible residual budget (@def-budget)                |
| $2\bar{d}_{\mathrm{res}} = 2c_x r^2/\gamma_0$ | ISS action ceiling (@thm-ceiling)                     |
